brief.headline: We are paying ₹385.00/KG for laminates — 54.0% above the ₹250.00/KG we pay Silk Polypack; target ₹250.00/KG to eliminate the ₹22718 annual excess.

priceAsk.target: ₹250.00/KG — the best price we currently pay (Silk Polypack) — closing the 54.0% gap and eliminating ₹22718 in annual excess cost
priceAsk.basis: Our current ₹385.00/KG is 54.0% above the ₹250.00/KG we pay Silk Polypack for the same laminate SKU, and 124% above the ₹171.60 ₹/kg import unit value for BOPET film substrate. We are overpaying by ₹22718 annually on a ₹64788 spend — a third of our total outlay with them.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 60 Days After Receipt to 30 days, or offer 15-day acceleration for an additional discount
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 30 days frees ₹5325 in working capital for us; a further 15-day improvement frees another ₹2663

brief.financialLeverage: Uflex carries debt at 1.25x debt-to-equity and posted a thin 4.1% net margin against a healthy 13.4% EBITDA margin, signaling interest and tax drag. They are growing fast at 35.5% per year on ₹16492.00 Cr revenue, so they value volume commitments. However, our ₹64788 spend is 0.00% of their revenue — we have no standalone leverage. Their C health score (54/100) and gearing mean they value cash flow, so faster payment can be traded for price. Push hard on price parity with our best supplier, but tie the ask to volume or payment-term sweeteners to make it worth their while.

evidence.point: We pay Uflex ₹385.00/KG for laminates while Silk Polypack charges us ₹250.00/KG for the identical SKU
The gap costs us ₹22718 annually in excess spend on this one laminate line
BOPET film import benchmark is far below our laminate price
Our total annual spend with Uflex is negligible to them
Uflex is leveraged and running a thin net margin despite strong EBITDA
Accelerating payment terms by 30 days releases working capital for FDC
evidence.figure: ₹5325 freed at 30 days; another ₹2663 at 15 days more

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets with B health rating

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong credible second-source for laminate volume

alternates.name: Amcor Flexibles India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Amcor's India operation offering high-end pharma laminates — premium tier but very reliable fallback

risks: At 0.00% of their revenue, we lack standalone negotiating power — they can easily walk away unless we bundle volume commitment or multi-year offtake.
Uflex's 1.25x debt-to-equity and C health score (54/100) require us to monitor supply continuity and qualify alternates in parallel.
Their 35.5% revenue growth and strong EBITDA margin mean they are not desperate for our small order — frame the ask around helping them fill capacity or win share-of-wallet, not charity.
We currently pay 60 Days After Receipt; any payment acceleration we offer must be explicitly traded for a price concession or we give away leverage for free.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value Uflex's scale and capability, but we're paying you ₹385.00/KG for laminates while our best supplier delivers the same material at ₹250.00/KG — we need to close that 54.0% gap to keep this partnership commercial.
